definition: Roof repair restores a roof's weatherproof barrier by fixing localized damage — leaks, missing or torn shingles, failed flashing, and cracked seals — without replacing the entire roof. It targets specific failure points to extend the service life of an otherwise sound roof.

signs: Brown or yellow ceiling and wall stains that spread or darken after rainfall indicate an active roof leak or trapped attic moisture — per GAF and This Old House inspection guidance.
Missing, cracked, or torn shingles expose the underlayment and the roof deck to wind-driven rain — per GAF inspection guidance.
Granule loss with sandy grit in gutters indicates shingles nearing end of life; granule loss exceeding 30% of the surface is the common rule-of-thumb for beyond repair — per GAF.

Rusted, lifted, or bent flashing at chimneys, walls, skylights, and valleys is the most common leak source, because flashing seals the roof transitions that an estimated 90–95% of leaks trace back to — an industry estimate attributed to the NRCA.
Daylight through the roof deck seen from inside the attic indicates holes in the decking and shingles, a sign that points toward replacement rather than a patch — per This Old House.
A sagging ceiling or roofline indicates sheathing decay from prolonged moisture and ranks as a structural priority — per GAF.
selectionCriteria: Active New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor registration with the Division of Consumer Affairs (N.J.S.A. 56:8-136) — this is a registration, NOT a license; New Jersey issues no roofing license. Verify the 13VH registration number, which must appear on the contract and in advertising (N.J.S.A. 56:8-144).
Commercial general liability insurance of at least $500,000 per occurrence (N.J.S.A. 56:8-142), verified directly through a Certificate of Insurance issued by the carrier — not just a verbal claim.
A written contract for any home-improvement work over $500 (N.J.A.C. 13:45A-16.2), with start/completion dates and the total price.
A detailed, itemized written estimate that separates materials and labor and clearly specifies the scope of work before any work begins.
Local references and an established local presence in Essex County, rather than out-of-area crews that move on after a storm season.

A thorough, documented assessment that traces the moisture path from ridge to eave to the root-cause detail (flashing, shingles, underlayment, pipe boot) and documents the damage with photographs — not a quote from the visible drip point alone.

technicalFacts.fact: Roughly 90–95% of roof leaks originate at flashing details and only 5–10% at the open shingle field, so a repair diagnoses the root cause before sealing the failed component; water enters at one detail and travels before showing as an interior stain.
technicalFacts.source: Industry estimate attributed to the NRCA (process per Integrity Home Exteriors / North Coast Roofing)

technicalFacts.fact: Repair favors an asphalt roof under 10–15 years old; repair when damage stays localized and covers under 25–30% of the roof area, replace when damage exceeds 25–30% of the area or one repair approaches 50% of replacement cost (the '25% rule' and '50% rule' are contractor-consensus thresholds).
Wind and hail are the largest homeowners-insurance claim type, affecting 2.8% of insured homes per year (about 1 in 36).

Repair or replacement of the roof covering on a detached one- and two-family dwelling counts as ordinary maintenance — no construction permit, inspection, or notice to the construction official required.
On a commercial building, repairing more than 25% of the total roof area in a 12-month period requires a permit.
Membrane life expectancy: EPDM lasts 15–25 years, TPO 7–20 years, and modified bitumen 20 years; EPDM fails most often at the seams while TPO fails at the welded seams.
Ponding water remaining on a low-slope roof more than 48 hours counts as a defect, and a flat roof needs at least 1/4 inch per foot of slope to drain.

A written workmanship warranty backs the labor, separate from the manufacturer material warranty that covers factory defects; membrane and low-slope systems use manufacturer-approved bonding rather than adhesive alone to keep a manufacturer system warranty intact.

The NRCA recommends a roof inspection twice per year — spring and fall — plus an inspection after any major storm, which aligns repair scheduling with lower-demand (and more competitively priced) seasons (late fall and early spring).

defabToKill.issue: Invented hyper-local climate stats stated as fact: 'northeasters with sustained 40-50 mph winds', freeze-thaw 'between November and March' as a mechanism, 'south-facing roof planes in Montclair and Bloomfield' UV degradation 'year-round', heating-bill spikes tied to ventilation. None of these wind speeds, month windows, or neighborhood-specific UV claims are in the gold.
defabToKill.fix: Ground each sign in the gold's 6 signs[] facts with named sources (GAF, This Old House, NRCA flashing estimate). Describe wind/freeze-thaw and UV qualitatively without fabricated mph, month ranges, or neighborhood-specific degradation rates.

defabToKill.issue: Mold-in-attic framed as a near-certain consequence of small leaks 'through a humid New Jersey summer' — overstated and unsourced.
defabToKill.fix: Keep attic moisture/staining as a grounded leak indicator (per GAF / This Old House). Do not assert mold as an inevitable outcome; if mentioned, treat it as a possible secondary problem without an invented prevalence.

defabToKill.issue: Vague code claim: 'New Jersey building code (N.J.A.C. 5:23) requires roofing systems to withstand specific wind uplift and snow load ratings' — no specific section, and conflates the code's scope.
defabToKill.fix: If code is cited at all, anchor it to the accurate ordinary-maintenance provision (N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7: detached 1- and 2-family roof-covering repair needs no permit). Do not invent wind-uplift/snow-load 'ratings' language.

defabToKill.issue: Fabricated, unsourced dollar tiers presented as NQR's own pricing: minor '$250-$750', moderate '$750-$2,500', major '$2,500-$7,000+', architectural shingles '$90-$110/square in 2022 now $120-$150/square', permits '$75-$200', and 'set aside $500-$1,000 annually'. The metaDescription even ranges '$250 to $7,000+'. None of these trace to a named source.
defabToKill.fix: Replace with the gold's sourced figures ONLY: roof-leak repair $400–$1,000 (HomeAdvisor/Modernize), flashing reseal $200–$500 (Modernize), valley repair $400–$1,000+ (HomeAdvisor), NJ 10–40% above national (Integrity Home Exteriors), emergency/after-hours +25–50% (Integrity Home Exteriors). Frame the overall as '$200–$1,000+ for most repairs' (a per-repair range, NOT a whole-job total) and end with a free written estimate. hasRealWholeProjectTotal is FALSE — do not present any single whole-job number.

defabToKill.issue: Fabricated company-scale claim: 'We have completed thousands of repairs across Newark, Montclair, and surrounding communities.'
defabToKill.fix: Remove the volume claim entirely. NQR is a roofing contractor / registered New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor serving Essex County — no 'thousands of repairs' figure.

defabToKill.issue: Credential error: 'NJ licensed contractors must pull these permits' and 'working with a licensed NJ contractor'. NJ issues no roofing license.
defabToKill.fix: Use 'registered New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor' (NEVER 'licensed'). Note that under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 a detached 1- and 2-family roof-covering repair is ordinary maintenance and needs no permit; do not assert a flat per-permit dollar amount.

defabToKill.issue: Manufacturer-certification self-claims presented as a contractor-quality signal: 'GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, and Owens Corning Preferred contractors... can offer enhanced warranty coverage'. NQR makes NO manufacturer-certification self-claim.
defabToKill.fix: Remove the certification-shopping advice entirely. Ground 'how to choose' in the verifiable selectionCriteria: active NJ HIC registration (13VH number, N.J.S.A. 56:8-136/144), CGL insurance min $500,000/occurrence verified by Certificate of Insurance (N.J.S.A. 56:8-142), written contract over $500 (N.J.A.C. 13:45A-16.2), itemized written estimate, local references, documented root-cause assessment.

defabToKill.issue: Unsupported NQR-specific insurance figure: 'We carry $2 million in general liability and full workers comp coverage.' Not substantiated in the gold (gold says only 'carries liability coverage').
defabToKill.fix: State NQR carries liability coverage as a registered NJ HIC (per the Contractors' Registration Act). Do not assert a specific $2M policy limit. Cite the legal minimum of $500,000/occurrence (N.J.S.A. 56:8-142) as what homeowners should verify, not an NQR-specific number.

defabToKill.issue: Wrong statute cited: 'New Jersey consumer protection law (N.J.S.A. 56:8-1) requires written contracts for home improvement work.' The written-contract requirement is N.J.A.C. 13:45A-16.2 (Home Improvement Practices regs), for work over $500.
defabToKill.fix: Cite N.J.A.C. 13:45A-16.2 — a written contract is required for home-improvement work over $500. Keep the Contractors' Registration Act for the registration/insurance points (N.J.S.A. 56:8-136/142/144).

defabToKill.issue: Fabricated portfolio/scale claims in body and CTA: 'We have repaired more storm-chaser-damaged roofs than we can count' and 'We are fully licensed, insured, and certified in New Jersey with hundreds of completed repairs across Essex County.'
defabToKill.fix: Drop the volume claims and 'fully licensed/certified'. NQR is a registered New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor, insured, serving Essex County. The storm-chaser warning is fine as advice (verify local presence, written contract, COI) — just without the 'more than we can count' self-claim.

defabToKill.issue: Implied 24/7 / always-available framing risk via 'do not let urgency push you'. (No explicit 24/7 claim present, but guard against adding one.)
defabToKill.fix: Do not introduce any '24/7' or after-hours promise — the gold only substantiates business hours (Mon–Fri 7:00 AM–6:00 PM, Sat 8:00 AM–2:00 PM). Emergency/after-hours work carries a +25–50% surcharge (Integrity Home Exteriors), it is not an always-on free service.

directAnswer must be TOPIC-definitional (what roof repair IS), not NQR-first; NQR appears only in ctaText. Ground every fact in the committed service-content/repair-maintenance.ts roof-repair gold block — do not invent.

hasRealWholeProjectTotal is FALSE for roof repair: the gold prices only per-repair components (leak $400–$1,000, flashing $200–$500, valley $400–$1,000+) with named sources. Do NOT synthesize these into a single whole-job total or invent a project total.

When citing GAF, This Old House, NRCA, Owens Corning, HomeAdvisor, Modernize, Integrity Home Exteriors, or InterNACHI, attribute them as external named sources for facts/guidance — NOT as NQR certifications, partnerships, or memberships.
